identity.name: SURAKSHA DIAGNOSTIC LTD
identity.industry: Diagnostics & Advanced Imaging / Eastern India Regional Leader

summary.oneLiner: Suraksha delivered robust 23% FY26 revenue growth driven by volume expansion and premium test mix (Genomics/Radiology), though EBITDA margins compressed 200bps to 31.8% due to new center ramp-up costs. The thesis hinges on operating leverage recovery as 14 new centers mature in FY27, targeting a 33% blended margin while expanding beyond West Bengal into adjacent states.

one-line thesis: Suraksha delivered robust 23% FY26 revenue growth driven by volume expansion and premium test mix (Genomics/Radiology), though EBITDA margins compressed 200bps to 31.8% due to new center ramp-up costs. The thesis hinges on operating leverage recovery as 14 new centers mature in FY27, targeting a 33% blended margin while expanding beyond West Bengal into adjacent states.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 3,136 Mn (+22.5% YoY); Q4 Rev: INR 822 Mn (+25% YoY). EBITDA: INR 986 Mn (+15.8% YoY); Margin: 31.8% (vs 33.8% FY25); Mature centers at 36-37%, New centers at -5.5%. PAT (Reported): INR 314 Mn (+1.4% YoY); PAT Margin: 10.1%. PAT (Normalized/Pre-Ind AS): ~INR 39-53 Cr (Management provided conflicting figures: CFO cited INR 53 Cr PAT impact, another exec cited INR 39 Cr PAT). Order Book: N/A (Service model). Net Debt: Not explicitly disclosed; Capex funded via internal accruals/debt not detailed. One-offs: Higher depreciation/finance costs from expansion; Election-related delays in center launches.
guidance: FY27 Revenue Growth: ~15% (conservative guidance despite 23% FY26 actuals). FY27 EBITDA Margin: ~33% (stabilizing from 31.8% as new centers mature). Order Inflow: Genomics run-rate INR 3.5 Mn/month. Capex: ~INR 70 Cr for 5 hubs + 8 spokes in FY27.
order book & pipeline: N/A for service business; Pipeline includes 14 new centers in FY27 (3 hubs/8 spokes in WB; 1 hub each in Bihar, Tripura, Jharkhand) targeting 82 total centers by FY27 end, 100 by FY28.
segment / subsidiary detail: Pathology (48.85% rev, high consumable cost); Radiology (44.26% rev, lower consumable/higher reporting cost, 1.5T helium-free MRI deployed); Consultancy (6.89% rev, 85% fee payout to doctors); Genomics (INR 1 Cr in Q4, INR 3.5 Mn/month run-rate, fast-turnaround NGS platform).
growth verticals / optionality: Geographic expansion into Bihar, Jharkhand, Tripura, and Assam (Guwahati traction); Genomics scaling (oncology/prenatal); AI integration (Alzheimer's detection pilot with IIT Kharagpur); Specialty clinics (Dementia, Epilepsy, Gyne-oncology).
margins & cost dynamics: Blended EBITDA margin 31.8% (-200bps YoY) due to new center pre-operating expenses and fixed cost absorption. Mature centers deliver 36-37% margins. New centers (<2 yrs) at -5.5% EBITDA. Breakeven: 5-6 months (small), 9-12 months (large) at center level; +1-2 quarters for HO expense absorption. Professional fees (doctors) ~16-17% of revenue (variable cost). Rental cost ~INR 30 Cr/year.
capex / expansion: FY27 planned capex ~INR 70 Cr for 5 hubs and 8 spokes. Recent investments include Genexus NGS platform, 1.5T helium-free MRI at Calcutta Medical College, Roche automation in pathology labs.
capital allocation: Focus on organic expansion (14 new centers FY27); Technology upgrades (Genomics, AI, MRI); No M&A mentioned; Dividend policy not discussed in transcript.
risks & watch-items: Execution risk on new center ramp-up (margin dilution); Regulatory delays (elections impacted licenses/power); Patient count metric reliability (management admits data hygiene issues); Competition in Eastern India; Dependence on West Bengal concentration (though diversifying).
management quality / tone: Confident on long-term structural growth and technology leadership; Conservative on short-term guidance (15% rev growth) to account for expansion drag; Transparent about margin compression being temporary due to ramp-up; Defensive on patient growth metrics citing data hygiene flaws.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly de-emphasizes 'patient count' growth as a flawed metric due to lack of unique IDs and IT consolidation efforts, shifting focus to revenue/patient (up to INR 2,264) and test volume. Pre-Ind AS PAT figures were contradictory during Q&A (CFO said INR 53 Cr, another exec said INR 39 Cr), suggesting potential accounting complexity or communication gaps. Genomics revenue is still nascent (INR 1 Cr in Q4) but positioned as a key future pillar with fastest TAT in Eastern India.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need for advanced, fast-turnaround genomic testing in Eastern India currently served by sending samples outside region. | Suraksha Diagnostic Ltd | beneficiary | High | Deployment of Genexus NGS platform reduces TAT from 14-21 days to 48-72 hours, capturing local demand and improving margins via premium pricing. |
| Radiologists and Pathologists seeking structured consultancy opportunities with guaranteed patient flow. | Local Medical Practitioners (Unlisted) | beneficiary | Med | Polyclinic model offers 85% fee retention for doctors, driving referral loyalty, though this caps Suraksha's margin in this segment. |
| Patients in Bihar, Jharkhand, Tripura lacking access to high-end diagnostics. | Suraksha Diagnostic Ltd | beneficiary | Med | First-mover advantage in setting up specialized hubs in these adjacent states leverages brand equity from West Bengal. |

themes.title: Hospitals, diagnostics & domestic healthcare
themes.need: Under-bedded India plus insurance penetration and preventive-care adoption drive a domestic healthcare capex + volume cycle distinct from export pharma. MAXHEALTH adding ~2,500+ beds (Gurgaon 500-bed by FY27); APOLLOHOSP/MEDANTA/KIMS/NH/ASTERDM/MAXHEALTH on hospitals; LALPATHLAB/METROPOLIS/THYROCARE/VIJAYA on diagnostics (LALPATHLAB guides 13-15% FY27); MEDPLUS/ENTERO on pharmacy/distribution; POLYMED on devices. The same India-only demand engine now also carries India-facing branded pharma, which is driven by domestic volume and price rather than the export book: GLAXO delivered its first INR 1,000cr quarter with 8.1% revenue growth, Shingrix at a ~INR 75cr annual run-rate (CY25, +80% YoY) and Jemperli's first-line approval expanding eligible patients from 800 to 6,000; ERIS (dermatology 15% of revenue after INR 1,265cr of domestic brand acquisitions), SANOFI (India-for-India, NLEM price cuts) and THEMISMED (hospital segment +20% YoY) sit on the same axis.
themes.driver: New-bed commissioning + occupancy ramp; Tier 3/4 diagnostics penetration; CGHS rate revision; preventive-test volumes; domestic branded-formulation volume growth and NLEM/price actions.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Describes itself as the 'Largest Integrated Diagnostic Chain in East India' with a dominant position, 'well-positioned to benefit from the high-growth opportunity for organized diagnostic chains in the fragmented markets in Eastern and North-Eastern India'.
- Integrated one-stop model offering pathology, radiology and medical consultation services under a single brand, versus standalone labs; hub centres offer pathology plus basic and advanced radiology while spokes offer pathology plus basic/intermediate radiology.
- Deeply concentrated in West Bengal - the deck states the state 'Accounted for 95.5% of FY26 Revenue from operations' and calls it the 4th most populous state in India with a fragmented market and low penetration of chained diagnostic centres.
- Consumer-led revenue mix: B2C Revenue was 91% in Q1 FY27, with 'high brand recall', high individual consumer business share and customer retention listed as strengths.
- First centre launched in 1992 under the 'Suraksha' brand; earlier backing from PE investors Lighthouse Funds and OrbiMed, IPO and listing on BSE and NSE, and exit of Lighthouse Funds are all shown on the milestone timeline.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisitions] The milestone timeline records acquisition of 2 pre-existing diagnostic centres in Kolkata from Future Medical & Research Trust and the acquisition of Fetomat Wellness Private Limited (63% stake); a negative non-controlling interest of Rs. (13.72) Mn at FY26 is consistent with a loss-making partly-owned subsidiary.
- [Shareholding] Shareholding pattern as at 30th June 2026 comprises Promoter & Promoter Group, DIIs, FIIs and Others; the extract lists the values 13.47%, 23.23%, 14.21% and 49.10% ahead of the labels FIIs, DIIs, Others and Promoter & Promoter Group, implying FIIs 13.47%, DIIs 23.23%, Others 14.21% and Promoter & Promoter Group 49.10%, but that pairing is by order and is not independently confirmed in the text.
- [Industry - CRISIL] Indian diagnostics market of INR 860-870 bn in FY24E is projected to reach INR 1,275-1,375 bn by FY28P (CAGR 10-12%), with pathology INR 480-490 bn to INR 700-755 bn (CAGR 9-11%) and radiology INR 375-385 bn to INR 570-620 bn (CAGR 11-13%); organized players are shown gaining share from standalone labs, with diagnostic chains moving from 13-17% (FY20) to 20-24% (FY24E) of the market.
- [Industry - East India] East (incl. North-East) India is presented as underserved yet premium priced: 0.96 NABL labs per mn population versus an all-India average of 1.61, 50 NABH accredited hospitals versus an average of 179, and average diagnostic test expenditure of INR 80-90 (highest, alongside West); the East India diagnostics market is projected at INR 170-180 bn (FY24E) to INR 260-280 bn (FY28P) and West Bengal at INR 61-63 bn to INR 95-100 bn, both at 10.5-12.5% CAGR.
- [Leadership] Both the Chairman & Joint Managing Director (Dr. Somnath Chatterjee, 33+ years) and the Joint Managing Director & CEO (Ritu Mittal, 29+ years) have been associated with Suraksha since incorporation; the wider board is majority independent and includes two chartered accountants and a company secretary.
